items.statement:
Let $U,V,a,b$ satisfy [[def-regular-minimum-energy-path-in-a-collision-free-tube]]. **Inputs:** an integer $M\ge2$, images $R_0=a,R_1,\ldots,R_M=b$ in $U$, spring constant $\kappa\ge0$, fixed step $\eta>0$, force and spacing tolerances $\tau_F,\tau_s\ge0$, an ordinary-step count $n_{\rm climb}\in\mathbb N_0$, and a finite update budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$. Require $n_{\rm climb}\le N$. **Output:** the last chain and one of `tolerances-met`, `tangent-failure`, `geometry-failure`, `nonfinite-evaluation`, or `budget-exhausted`.

At each iteration, endpoints are fixed and only interior images are updated. First evaluate $V_i=V(R_i)$ for every image; if any energy is nonfinite, return `nonfinite-evaluation` before making energy comparisons. For $i=1,\ldots,M-1$, write $\Delta_i^+=R_{i+1}-R_i$ and $\Delta_i^-=R_i-R_{i-1}$. Select an unnormalized tangent by

$$\tau_i=\begin{cases}\Delta_i^+,&V_{i+1}>V_i>V_{i-1},\\\Delta_i^-,&V_{i+1}<V_i<V_{i-1},\\w_{\max}\Delta_i^+ + w_{\min}\Delta_i^-,&\text{otherwise and }V_{i+1}>V_{i-1},\\w_{\min}\Delta_i^+ + w_{\max}\Delta_i^-,&\text{otherwise and }V_{i+1}<V_{i-1},\\\Delta_i^++\Delta_i^-,&V_{i+1}=V_{i-1},\end{cases}$$

where $w_{\max}=\max(|V_{i+1}-V_i|,|V_{i-1}-V_i|)$ and $w_{\min}=\min(|V_{i+1}-V_i|,|V_{i-1}-V_i|)$. When $V_{i+1}=V_{i-1}$, the displayed centered-chord branch is the algorithm's explicit tie convention; it is a local completion of the strict-comparison rule in the cited improved-tangent formula. If $\tau_i=0$, return `tangent-failure`; otherwise set $t_i=\tau_i/\|\tau_i\|_2$. Next evaluate $\nabla V(R_i)$ for every interior image; if any gradient is nonfinite, return `nonfinite-evaluation` before forming forces.

Initialize the update counter $k=0$. At iteration $k$, use the ordinary force

$$F_i=-(I-t_it_i^T)\nabla V(R_i)+\kappa(\|\Delta_i^+\|_2-\|\Delta_i^-\|_2)t_i.$$

When $k\ge n_{\rm climb}$, choose the least index $i_*$ attaining the largest interior energy and replace that image's force by

$$F_{i_*}^{\rm CI}=-\nabla V(R_{i_*})+2(\nabla V(R_{i_*})^Tt_{i_*})t_{i_*};$$

the climbing image has no spring force. The remaining interior images retain the ordinary force. If any resulting force is nonfinite, return `nonfinite-evaluation`. Thus iterations $k=0,\ldots,n_{\rm climb}-1$ use ordinary forces and the first climbing force is evaluated at iteration $k=n_{\rm climb}$. At each iteration report the maximum force norm and spacing residual $\max_i|\|\Delta_i^+\|_2-\|\Delta_i^-\|_2|$. Stop with `tolerances-met` only if both are within their declared tolerances. If a tolerance fails and $k=N$, return `budget-exhausted`; only when $k<N$ update every interior image by $R_i^{k+1}=R_i^k+\eta F_i^k$. Leaving $U$ returns `geometry-failure`. After a valid update set $k\leftarrow k+1$ and repeat. The tolerance check precedes the budget check, so $N=0$ still checks the initial chain and $n_{\rm climb}=N$ uses a climbing force at the final residual check (without an update if the budget is then exhausted).

The finite stopping status does not assert convergence to a MEP, a saddle, or a continuum path.

items.statement:
Let $U,V$ be as in [[def-regular-minimum-energy-path-in-a-collision-free-tube]]. **Inputs:** an initial point $x_0\in U$, a unit initial mode reference $v_{\rm ref}\in\mathbb R^d$, a local-ball center $x_{\rm ref}\in U$, radius $r_{\rm loc}>0$, gradient tolerance $\tau_g\ge0$, eigenvalue margin $\gamma>0$, eigenpair residual tolerance $\tau_{\rm eig}\ge0$, mode-overlap threshold $0\le\tau_{\rm mode}<1$, update budget $N\in\mathbb N_0$, and a supplied spectral-data routine $E$. On input $(x,H(x))$, $E$ must return in finite time either `failure` or an orthogonal matrix $Q$, ordered approximate eigenvalues $\widehat\lambda_j$, and validated ordered intervals $I_j$ with their checked certificates as specified below. This input routine supplies spectral data; the enclosure definition does not compute them. Return the last point, the most recently accepted mode reference, and a termination status from `geometry-failure`, `outside-local-basin`, `gradient-residual-tolerance`, `budget-exhausted`, `eigensolve-tolerance-failure`, `index-one-branch-failure`, `mode-tracking-failure`, or `singular-jacobian`. The mode reference starts at $v_{\rm ref}$ and changes only after a successful eigenpair and overlap check; it certifies the current lowest-mode line only when that check has passed at the current iterate. When called at $x_k$ in step 2, the input routine $E$ supplies an orthogonal matrix $Q=[q_1,\ldots,q_d]$, ordered approximate eigenvalues $\widehat\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\widehat\lambda_d$, and validated intervals $I_j=[\ell_j,u_j]$ in the sense of [[def-validated-eigenvalue-enclosures-for-an-index-one-hessian]]. Require every residual $\|H(x_k)q_j-\widehat\lambda_jq_j\|_2\le\tau_{\rm eig}$, $\sqrt d\,\tau_{\rm eig}\le\gamma/2$, and $\widehat\lambda_j\in I_j$. The Hessian $H=\nabla^2V$ is symmetric by [[cor-hessian-is-symmetric]].

For $k=0,\ldots,N$, in order:

1. If $x_k\notin U$, return `geometry-failure`. If $x_k\notin B_2(x_{\rm ref},r_{\rm loc})$, return `outside-local-basin`. Compute $g_k=\nabla V(x_k)$. If $\|g_k\|_2\le\tau_g$, return `gradient-residual-tolerance`; if $k=N$, return `budget-exhausted`.
2. Evaluate $H(x_k)$ and call $E(x_k,H(x_k))$. If it returns `failure`, return `eigensolve-tolerance-failure`; otherwise use its returned $Q$, $\widehat\lambda_j$, and $I_j$. If an eigenpair residual exceeds $\tau_{\rm eig}$, $\sqrt d\tau_{\rm eig}>\gamma/2$, or some $\widehat\lambda_j\notin I_j$, return `eigensolve-tolerance-failure`. If the validated intervals do not satisfy $u_1\le-\gamma$ and $\ell_j\ge\gamma$ for all $j\ge2$ (with the dimension-one convention in the definition), return `index-one-branch-failure`. If $|q_1^Tv_{\rm ref}|\le\tau_{\rm mode}$, return `mode-tracking-failure`; otherwise retain $q_1$ when $q_1^Tv_{\rm ref}>0$ and replace it by $-q_1$ when $q_1^Tv_{\rm ref}<0$. Use the resulting direction as the next mode reference. This overlap check detects a mode-branch change but does not alter the Newton correction.
3. Call [[alg-newton-correction-for-vector-residuals]] with $A=H(x_k)$ and $r=g_k$. If it returns `singular-jacobian`, return that status. Its correction $p_k$ is the exact Newton solution of $H(x_k)p_k=-g_k$ in the mathematical model; the eigenpair data certifies the index-one branch but does not replace this linear solve.
4. If $x_k+p_k\notin U$ or lies outside $B_2(x_{\rm ref},r_{\rm loc})$, return `outside-local-basin`. Otherwise set $x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k$ and continue.

An approximate eigensolve has a finite residual-tolerance branch and an explicit failure status. The definition makes no global-convergence claim. Local quadratic behavior is stated separately and requires the hypotheses of [[thm-updated-jacobian-newton-local-quadratic-convergence]].

items.title: Centered-tangent string residuals are second-order consistent on a regular MEP
A separated dimer mode gives a local inexact saddle error bound
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, and let $V\in C^4(U,\mathbb R)$ using the convention of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. Fix $x\in U$. Put $H=\nabla^2V(x)$ and suppose a validated ordered eigenvalue enclosure certifies index one with gap $\gamma>0$ as in [[def-validated-eigenvalue-enclosures-for-an-index-one-hessian]], so $\lambda_1(H)\le-\gamma$ and $\lambda_j(H)\ge\gamma$ for $j\ge2$. Let $\epsilon>0$, let $v$ be a unit direction accepted by the rotation test of [[alg-finite-budget-dimer-mode-following]], and assume the whole segment $x+[-\epsilon,\epsilon]v$ lies in $U$. Let $D_\epsilon$ be the paired-force estimate, with $\|(I-vv^T)D_\epsilon\|_2\le\tau_{\rm rot}$. Suppose each force evaluation has Euclidean error at most $\eta$ and the third derivatives of each gradient coordinate along this segment are bounded by $M_4$. Set

$$\delta:=\frac{\sqrt d\,M_4}{6}\epsilon^2+\frac{\eta}{\epsilon}.$$

If $\delta\le\gamma/4$ and the measured Rayleigh estimate $v^TD_\epsilon\le-\gamma/2$, then the sine of the angle from $v$ to the lowest-eigenvalue line of $H$ satisfies

$$\sin\angle(v,q_1):=\sqrt{1-|q_1^Tv|^2}\le\frac{4(\tau_{\rm rot}+\delta)}{5\gamma},$$

where $q_1$ is any unit eigenvector for $\lambda_1(H)$. This is a conditional mode bound; rotation success alone is not an index certificate.

Let $\epsilon_g=\|\nabla V(x)\|_2$. If $\epsilon_g=0$, $x$ itself is an index-one critical point. If $\epsilon_g>0$, put $\rho=2\epsilon_g/\gamma$ and additionally assume $B_2(x,2\rho)\subset U$, $H(\cdot)=\nabla^2V(\cdot)$ is $L$-Lipschitz in the induced Euclidean operator norm on that ball, and $L\rho/\gamma\le1/2$. Then there is a unique index-one critical point $x_*$ in $\overline B_2(x,\rho)$ and

$$\|x_*-x\|_2\le\rho=\frac{2\epsilon_g}{\gamma}.$$

The dimer direction bound does not replace the validated eigenvalue enclosure or the residual, inverse, and Hessian-Lipschitz conditions in this local saddle certificate.
